summary: The fair scheduler's figures on four processors, against Linux 6.12's: shares, wakes, the real-time class, the fair server, priority inheritance, balance and suspend

cases.behavior: The fair scheduler on four processors as Linux 6.12 schedules: shares by nice value, SCHED_IDLE and session with autogroup on and off, the wait of a thread that sleeps often, RR's 100 ms turns, the fair server's 5%, a priority-inheriting futex owner, balance under load, a pull by an idle processor and a suspend to idle with threads queued and delayed

execution.cleanup: kill every spinner, reap each child and session leader, and put back kernel.sched_autogroup_enabled and kernel.sched_schedstats on every exit

assertions.checks: Processors 0 to 3 are allowed, the program runs as root and /proc/self/sched shows se.sum_exec_runtime
A nice-0 and a nice-5 spinner pinned to processor 1 in one session share it 1024:335 within 5%, by se.sum_exec_runtime over 10 s after 2 s of warm-up
A nice-19 and a SCHED_IDLE spinner pinned to processor 2 share it 15:3 within 5%, by se.sum_exec_runtime over 10 s after 2 s of warm-up
With kernel.sched_autogroup_enabled at 1, a session of one spinner and a session of four, all pinned to processor 3, share it half and half within 5%
With kernel.sched_autogroup_enabled at 0, the same two sessions share processor 3 in the ratio 1:4 within 5%

With kernel.sched_schedstats at 1, a process pinned to processor 1 that sleeps 1 ms and runs 0.1 ms 2000 times, beside a nice-0 spinner on each processor, has a wait_count of at least 2000 and a wait_sum over wait_count at most 25% or 0.5 ms above Debian's, whichever is larger: -w gives Debian's 126,777 ns, the median of three runs of the same program on Debian 13's 6.12.115 in this profile under KVM, in the root cgroup, on 2026-11-19

sched_rr_timeslice_ms reads 100 and sched_rr_get_interval gives 100 ms for a SCHED_RR process, and two equal SCHED_RR spinners pinned to processor 3 run in turns of 100 ms within 10%, by se.sum_exec_runtime over nr_involuntary_switches, and share it half and half within 5%
A SCHED_FIFO spinner pinned to processor 2 leaves a nice-0 spinner beside it 5% of the processor within one percentage point, the fair server's 50 ms of each 1000 ms

An ordinary thread holding a priority-inheriting mutex on processor 1, held off by a SCHED_FIFO spinner there, reads prio 79 in its /proc sched file with policy 0 while a SCHED_FIFO waiter of priority 20 waits, and lets the mutex go to the waiter

Eight spinners started on processor 1 and then allowed all four get four processors' worth of run time within 10% over 6 s after 2 s, each within 25% of their mean, and migrate six times or more in all

With processor 2 idle, a spinner allowed processors 1 and 2 beside one pinned to processor 1 migrates at least once, and both run at least 90% of 3 s after 1 s, which only a pull to processor 2 can give them

A write of freeze to /sys/power/state, with the clock's alarm 3 s ahead, while two spinners share processor 1 and a process that runs 0.5 ms between sleeps of 0.2 ms shares processor 2 with a spinner, lets none of them run more than 200 ms until the alarm; afterwards each runs again and the two on processor 1 share it half and half within 10%
Every process the test made is killed and reaped, and the sysctls it changed are put back

native.reason: each row judges how processors 1 to 3 are shared, which the installed system's services move, and the wake row compares with Debian's figure in the same four-processor QEMU profile
